quote.text: What does a babysitter or grandparent need to know about my child

promise.text: Babysitter information sheet: what to put on it

lines.text: A one-page sheet for a sitter or grandparent: allergies first, medicines, who to call, your address and bedtime notes.

eyebrow.text: Set it up in this order

head.text: Write the allergies first and put them in a box.

body.text: Say what happens in your own words: "peanuts, hives" is clearer than "nut allergy."

eyebrow.text: Set it up in this order

head.text: Copy the medicine line from the label, not from memory: name, dose, how often.

body.text: If a medicine is only given some days, say which.

eyebrow.text: Set it up in this order

head.text: Add two numbers for you and a second adult, and say which to call first.

body.text: A second name helps when your phone is in a movie theater.

eyebrow.text: Set it up in this order

head.text: Write the address and the nearest cross street.

body.text: A sitter shouldn't have to read the mailbox in a hurry, and a caller to 911 needs it.

eyebrow.text: Set it up in this order

head.text: Add the doctor's name and number, and a poison control number.

body.text: The National Capital Poison Center's site lists 1-800-222-1222 as a free, expert and confidential line.

line.text: A Caregiver sheet: allergies first, what is taken, who to call, and your own notes about bedtime, comforts and fears.
